market_holds: The Q3 numbers are already public. Opera pre-announced them on 2026-11-03 (6-K): revenue $182.8m (+20% y/y, top of the $181-183m guide), adjusted EBITDA $43.2m (above the $41-43m guide), IFRS net income $27.6m and desktop MAU at 100m. The stock rose 4.5% that day and then gave it back. In the same release the CFO said the company will approach its 'final Q4 guidance with prudence'. Consensus: FY26 revenue is $740m on stockanalysis (7 analysts) and about $738m on Earnings Whispers (2026-11-10). Q1-Q3 sum to $536.6m, so consensus implies Q4 of about $201-203m (+14-15% y/y on Q4'25's $177.2m). FY27 consensus is $853m (+15%). The company's own FY guide of $734-742m (2026-08-19) implies Q4 of $197.4-205.4m (+11.4% to +15.9%). Price: $15.43 at the seal. The stock is -12.5% over 20 days, -24.9% from its 52-week high and about -15% since the August print. Most of the October fall was GOOGL's -12.6% on 2026-10-29, after Alphabet's ad miss, plus Nasdaq weakness: OPRA fell 6.8% on 10-29 and 11.3% on 10-30, and QQQ fell 3.5% on 10-30 and 6.5% on 11-05. QQQ is -2.4% today. Options: front expiry 11-20 at 103% ATM IV. That is roughly an 8-9% straddle by my arithmetic, but the ATM spread is 104% of mid, so the number is unreliable. Calls are richer (25d skew -15.6 vol points). Usual move: median 4.9% over 8 events. The guide-day reactions were -3.4% close on Q3'25 (2025-10-29, Q4 guided at +11-13%), +5.3% on Q1'26, -7.1% on Q2'26 (beat and raise) and +23.4% on Q4'25/FY26 guide plus the $300m buyback. Sell-side targets average about $26 (Investing.com, around 11-10). Kunlun owns 67.9% (13D/A of 2026-09-22), so the float is small. The trading line is the Q4 guide, FY narrowing and the Google renewal, not Q3.
view: With Q3 pre-announced, tomorrow's release carries little news on the quarter. It turns on the Q4 guide, the FY range, any 2027 or Google commentary, and capital return. Opera guides Q4 very conservatively. Last year it guided Q4 at +11-13% while Q3 grew 23%, then delivered +22%. The CFO has already told the market on 11-03 to expect 'prudence'. If Opera repeats last year's habit, the Q4 guide lands around $195-200m and the FY narrows to roughly $733-737m. That is a hair below the $738-740m consensus and could read as a trimmed top end. That is a mild negative against a sell-side number that still sits about +15% for Q4. The other overhang is the Google search agreement: the ex-US term ends 2026-12-31 and the US term ends 2027-01-31 (20-F). A renewal announced with the results would be a strong upside surprise, but past renewals came in December or April, so I put it at a minority probability. A call answer of 'in discussions' keeps the overhang. Against the negative lean: the stock is already down 15% since August at about 7x EV/EBITDA. The pre-warning has been public for two weeks. Opera's sandbagging is well known. Buyback acceleration is plausible with $270m+ of authorization left. Nasdaq beta is high and dominates a move to 13:00. Net: a mild lean down, not a bet.
unpriced: Probably a small gap between consensus Q4 revenue (about $203m, +14.8% y/y, implied by FY $740m) and what Opera's own guiding habit plus the CFO's 'prudence' remark imply (about $195-200m). The consensus looks stale against the company's own warning. That gap is small, partly offset by the stock's two-week underperformance, and it competes with a possible Google-renewal or buyback surprise. Not enough to act on.

recommendation.reason: The quarter is already public, so the release turns on a Q4 guide the company has pre-flagged as prudent. Its habit (Q4'25 guided +11-13% after a +23% Q3) points to a guide a little under the roughly +15% consensus. That is a real but small and partly visible gap. A possible Google renewal, buyback news and heavy Nasdaq beta to 13:00 keep the direction well under 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Google search agreement renewal (ex-US beyond 2026-12-31) announced with the results, or a Q4 guide at or above about $203m (FY raised to $740m+), would make the stock likely higher.

self_critique: Opera's conservative guiding is so well known that analysts may already model below the FY midpoint in their Q4 numbers. The $740m FY consensus could be stale headline data rather than live expectations. The stock already fell 15% into the print at about 7x EV/EBITDA, and the 'prudence' warning has been public for two weeks. A guide in line with the warning could produce a relief rally, especially with buyback news, a dividend or a positive Google update. Market beta (QQQ swinging 2-6% a day) could swamp any guide effect by 13:00.
approach_notes: Writing down what the price holds first was decisive here: it showed the quarter was pre-announced and moved the question to the guide. Finding the cause of the October fall needed peer bars, not news searches; searching news for a price move wasted several queries.
